reason: The hypothesis directly restates the findings and proposed future work of P1 and P2, which already demonstrated that boron addition to AlCoCrFeNiMoTi forms TiB2, refines the microstructure, and improves both wear and corrosion resistance. The mechanism linking TiB2 to dislocation blocking and passive film stabilization is taken from P1 and P9, and the predicted outcomes mirror the reported results in P1 and P11. The only new element is the explicit combination of wear and corrosion in a single simultaneous test, which P1 already implies as a future direction.
copied_elements: Boron microalloying of AlCoCrFeNiMoTi HEA via laser cladding
In situ formation of TiB2 particles
TiB2 particles as barriers to dislocation motion
Enhanced passive film stability at low B content
Reduced corrosion current density (icorr) with small B addition
